four distinct collinear points or six points which are pairwise visible with

composing the tree leaves only Lean's standard logical axioms.

times as many edges as vertices, then the `(r+1)`-admissibility of `G` is

proofs.description:
Every nowhere dense graph class has subpolynomial density: for every
depth `r` and every `ε > 0` there is a constant `c` such that every
depth-`r` minor of a member, on `m` vertices, has at most `c * m^(1+ε)`
edges.

proofs.description:
Every nowhere dense graph class is uniformly quasi-wide: for every radius
`r` there are a threshold function `N` and a separator bound `s` such that
in every member, every vertex set of size at least `N m` contains a
distance-`r` independent subset of size at least `m` after deleting at
most `s` vertices.
proofs.tooltipHtml: Every nowhere dense graph class is uniformly quasi-wide: for every radius rrr there are a threshold function NNN and a separator bound sss such that in every member, every vertex set of size at least NmN mNm contains a distance-rrr independent subset of size at least mmm after deleting at most sss vertices.

every subgraph `H` of a member, on `m` vertices, satisfies

proofs.description:
Model checking monadic second-order logic is linear time on a word
random access machine for graphs presented together with a

program which, on a compressed sparse row block followed by a

length of the input, at every word length at which that constant
multiple of the length and of each entry of the input fits into a word.

proofs.description:
The Moser--Tardos witness-tree argument.  An infinite table supplies every
fresh sample used by the algorithm.  Each resampling occurrence injects into
a proper witness tree, the probability that a fixed tree occurs is the
product of its event probabilities, and the branching-process estimate sums
these products.  Finiteness of that sum also yields a terminating table and
hence an assignment avoiding all bad events.

proofs.description:
At the first stage where the observed event is true, adjoin it as a
distinguished root to the execution history.  The resulting proper witness
tree has no further copy of the root and all of its other labels lie in
`Gamma(B)`.  The witness-tree lemma bounds the probability of every such
tree, and the branching-process sum is exactly the local-lemma neighborhood
product.  The output event is a subset of the event that the observation was
true at some stage.

Every nowhere dense graph class is uniformly quasi-wide: for every radius
`r` there are a threshold function `N` and a separator bound `s` such that
in every member, every vertex set of size at least `N m` contains a
distance-`r` independent subset of size at least `m` after deleting at
most `s` vertices.
